one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company catalyst falls between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-29. Q1 FY27 results come in late November or around Dec 1 (Q1 FY26 was reported Nov 20, 2025), and the FY27 guide (Aug 25) was reaffirmed at the Sept Investor Day. The Oct 15 extension deadline and the Oct 16 dividend payment don't move the numbers. Unscheduled risks in the window are AI tax or bookkeeping agent launches ahead of the 2027 season, class-action news and broker target cuts, plus possible HRB/peer read-across. The stock is at its June low after a round trip from $268 to $367 and back, and reversal versus momentum roughly cancel. I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at about $268.5 (a small tilt from the $5B+/yr buyback) with a 1-month sigma of about 13.5%, slightly below 50%/3.5 since there is no event in the window. That is a touch wider on the left than round 1 because the IRS-versus-TurboTax share-loss datum makes negative industry headlines more credible.

fair_value.method: Blend (50/50) of 12.5x FY28 SBC-inclusive EPS of ~$25.5 (-> $319) and an 8% yield on normalized FY28 SBC-burdened FCF of ~$25.0/share (-> $313), about $316 at Sept 2027. The FCF leg now strips the one-off $1.28B OBBBA deferred-tax add-back from FY26 OCF.

inputs_detail.derivation: $5B+/yr of buybacks at ~$268 retires about 6-7% gross, less about 2.5-3% SBC issuance. FY26 cut the diluted average by only 2% because it bought at much higher prices.

FY27 guide $23.00 grown about 11%: about 7% net-income growth (revenue +8%, with GBS +12-13% and Consumer +2-4% as TurboTax keeps losing share at the low end) plus about 4% net share reduction. The +23-24% FY27 growth rate is not repeated because it is flattered by the restructuring. HRB expects industry filing growth to moderate in 2027, which caps TurboTax unit growth.

Cut from 13x. The ex-growth tax comparable H&R Block trades at about 6.6x forward ($40.58 vs FY27 adj. EPS guide $6.04-6.24), and IRS data shows TurboTax lost about 3.7 points of relative share in the 2026 season. INTU still earns a premium over HRB for 8-10% revenue growth, a 60%+ GBS mix and heavy buybacks, but I no longer give a premium over today's ~11.6x beyond what the re-accelerating EPS base justifies. Historical 30x+ multiples are not reachable within 12 months given the AI cost-per-return argument (Goldman $0.12 vs $162 ARPC).

bear.story: In the 2027 season TurboTax units fall again while the IRS self-prepared category grows slowly (HRB guides to moderating industry growth). AI agents (Perplexity, ChatGPT/Claude-based) and free tiers take the low end, and Intuit's own free entry points (Credit Karma Tax) cannibalize ARPC. QuickBooks net adds slow under AI bookkeeping competition. FY28 EPS comes in around $21 and the multiple compresses to about 7.8x, between HRB's 6.6x and 9x, on terminal-decline fears.

base.story: TurboTax revenue is flat to +3%, with share loss continuing at a slower pace at the low end. GBS grows 12-13% and Credit Karma is steady. About 4%/yr net buyback accretion gets FY28 EPS to about $25, and the multiple stays near 12x.

bull.story: The 2027 season shows TurboTax units matching or beating IRS self-prep growth (price cuts and AI features stop the churn, and AI rivals stay stuck at drafting rather than e-filing). QBO Advanced and Intuit Assist monetize. FY28 EPS reaches about $26.5 and the multiple re-rates to about 16x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $195 the stock is about 8.5x FY27 guided SBC-inclusive EPS and an ~11% normalized SBC-burdened FCF yield. At that level the market would be pricing an earnings decline, not just a de-rating: a failed 2027 tax season with TurboTax units down again against a growing self-prepared category, a guide cut at Q2/Q3 FY27, or QuickBooks customer growth turning negative. I lowered it from $200 because H&R Block's ~6.6x forward multiple shows an ex-growth tax franchise can re-rate lower than I assumed. Ordinary volatility can therefore reach $200-210 without anything breaking, and a trade toward $150-160 (an HRB-like multiple on flat EPS) would confirm the break.

Whether AI agents move from drafting returns to e-filing and take DIY share at scale in the 2027 season

reasoning: Round 2 revision. Industry-chain evidence, reread with the supervisor's fact-checks: IRS self-prepared e-file grew 1.7% to 65.73M through May 8, 2026 while TurboTax online units fell 2%. That is about 3.7 points of relative share loss in one season, so the category is healthy but Intuit is losing share, mostly at the price-sensitive end (the CEO says price is the number one churn reason). H&R Block's FY26 call (Aug 11) says it maintained, rather than gained, assisted share, expects 2027 industry growth to moderate but stay positive on slower job growth, and flags low-cost/free DIY competition. HRB trades at only about 6.6x forward EPS, a lower ex-growth floor than I had assumed. Direct File remains suspended. AI rivals are cheap (Goldman: $0.12 per return vs $162 ARPC), which argues for continued price compression rather than collapse inside 12 months. I verified in the 8-K that FY26 OCF of $8,838M includes a +$1,279M deferred-tax add-back (OBBBA R&D catch-up). Stripping it gives normalized SBC-burdened FCF of about $5.2B, not the ~$6.9B+ my round-1 FCF leg implied, although I had haircut it. I also corrected SBC: $2.0B pre-tax, with $5.81 the after-tax EPS effect. Offsetting this, buybacks at $268 retire about 4%/yr net (267.2M shares on Aug 31). Fair value: 12.5x FY28 EPS of $25.5 = $319 and 8% on ~$25.0 FCF/share = $313, blend ~$316 (from $322). Scenarios: bear $165 (28%), base $295 (50%), bull $425 (22%), mean ~$287. For the ladder I use a lognormal with median ~$285, sigma 0.44 below the median and 0.40 above, with a slightly fatter far-left tail for the HRB-multiple floor, giving P(>=268) = 0.555 (from 0.58). I disagree with nothing material in the supervisor's findings. I keep FY28 EPS at $25.5 on my own build, and I weight the share-loss datum a little more heavily in the bear probability than the supervisor did. Research this round: an SEC 8-K recheck and 3 web queries.
